key_insight: Machine learning applied to dried-serum Raman spectra showed promising discrimination between bladder cancer and symptomatic controls in a retrospective proof-of-concept study.
clinical_relevance: This blood-based approach could help prioritize patients for cystoscopy, but its clinical role remains unproven.
method: Analysed archived serum using dried-serum Raman spectroscopy.
Used supervised machine learning to estimate bladder cancer probabilities.
Evaluated ROC performance with and without age.
evidence_signal: Among 49 bladder cancer patients and 97 symptomatic controls, classifier AUC was approximately 0.90, increasing to approximately 0.91 with age.
watch_item: Prospective validation is needed to establish sensitivity at clinically relevant triage thresholds before considering implementation.
paper_title: Serum Raman spectroscopy as a blood-based triage test for bladder cancer: a retrospective proof-of-concept study
